A native iPad app (Videos, Map and Chat, offline, with optional on-device AI) is in mobile/ipad/. It is source for contributors to build and sign themselves.

new.description: File browser, app data manager and cache cleaner for iOS 26 and 27 (worse_query, no jailbreak)
new.readme: WQ Files is a file browser, app data manager and cache cleaner for iOS 26 and 27. "WQ" stands for worsequery, the sandbox technique it is built on. It reaches other apps' and system containers with no jailbreak and no kernel exploit. Tested on iOS 26.5 to the 27.3 beta; see Tested devices. iOS 26 (26.0 to 26.7.2): supported since 0.7; tested on 26.7.1.

new.description: Show the battery level of wireless mice, headsets, keyboards and controllers on the Windows 10/11 taskbar. Lightweight tray app, no vendor software needed. Supports Logitech, Razer, SteelSeries, Corsair, HyperX, Glorious, PS4/PS5 DualSense, Xbox and Bluetooth devices.
new.readme: Battery levels of your wireless mouse, headset, keyboard and controller, right on the Windows taskbar. Tiny: a ~350 KB app using about 2 MB of RAM. It's plain C++/Win32, with no runtime and no background service, and installs in seconds without admin rights. No vendor software needed: it talks to the devices directly. G HUB, Synapse, iCUE, GG and NGenuity can stay closed (or keep running; they don't conflict).

new.description: A live map beside the chat that shows what Claude Code is doing: tool calls, model steps, hooks, skills and subagents light up as they happen. Local only, in 7 languages.
new.readme: A mod for Claude Code: a live map of the work, in a pane beside the chat. Every tool call, model step, hook and skill sends a pulse from the centre to its station, so you see memory, files, shell, web and agents at work instead of reading a list of commands. It runs on your machine and sends nothing anywhere. Local does not mean blind: like any mod that follows tool calls it is handed each call whole, and it takes names from that and nothing else. What it reads and keeps, and the checks that hold it to that.

new.description: Source-built, locally bound FailSafe distribution of ARTEX (v0.3.15)
new.readme: A source-built, locally bound distribution of ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent security testing harness. This repository exists because the prebuilt tomicdd/artex Docker image was found to contain an unauthenticated command-execution backdoor in November 2026. This build is compiled from the audited v0.3.15 source tag and keeps upstream's full runtime capabilities, including Node 22, Playwright, Chromium, and nmap.

new.description: The open-source Dynamic Island for React, installed with shadcn.
new.readme: A Dynamic Island-style component for any React app, installed with shadcn. Show an upload, a timer, a song, a ride on its way, an incoming call or a recording in one island at the top of your app, and shape each activity around your app's own actions. The engine (lib/island/, registry item island-core): the activity stack, four presentations (idle, compact, the split, expanded), springs fitted to frame-by-frame recordings of the real island, long-press, alerts and reduced motion. React only.

new.description: STE80 Humanizer: agent skill that removes AI tells and rewrites text 80% of the way to ASD-STE100 (Simplified Technical English), the method Andrej Karpathy shared.
new.readme: Built by the team behind Dodaios, the open-source assistant that runs your coding agents for you. STE80 Humanizer makes AI-written text read like a careful person wrote it, without changing what it says. It combines two methods: The humanizer method. Remove the 26 tells from Wikipedia's Signs of AI writing, in the catalog of blader/humanizer. Karpathy's STE80 method. Rebuild the sentences "80% of the way to ASD-STE100", the controlled English of aircraft maintenance manuals.

new.description: AI clipping for long videos and live streams. Self-hosted, bring your own AI key.
new.readme: Turn long videos and live streams into captioned vertical clips, ready to post. Free and open source: run it on your own computer or server, with your own AI key. Paste a YouTube, Twitch or Kick link (or upload a file) and PeakCut finds the moments worth clipping, cuts them to 9:16, adds word-by-word captions and a hook, and can post them to your connected accounts. It can also record a creator's live stream and clip the highlights while the stream is still running. Clips from any video.

items.title: Remote Claude Code fleets in AWS get a learning loop that lowers cost
items.connection: Claude Code on Bedrock AgentCore runs isolated remote sessions with no cost figures, and TokenEconomizer learns from repository sessions to cut cost, so a fleet working the same repositories feeds the plugin more sessions to learn from.
items.context: Finance teams usually block agent scale-up until cost per task is known
chain: AgentCore gives enterprises a controlled place to run many Claude Code sessions that return pull requests.
TokenEconomizer learns short facts and failing loops from sessions on a repository, so more sessions should mean more to learn from.
Cost per pull request can fall as the fleet grows instead of staying flat.
Platform teams get a cost curve they can show finance, which unblocks budgeted scale-up.
items.who: AWS platform teams running internal coding agents benefit; central engineering budgets pay.
items.variable: Cost per merged agent pull request
items.versus: Running remote sessions without it leaves repeated failing loops and unused tools in every session, and the AWS guide gives no cost controls of its own.
items.smallest_test: Run a batch of similar tasks on one repository through AgentCore with and without the plugin; succeed if mean cost falls within the 18.4% to 30.9% range reported and merge rate does not drop.
items.disconfirm: Savings shrink or vanish in isolated remote sessions because learned facts do not persist across them.

items.title: CI security fix gates can follow written team rules, not only model judgment
items.connection: On 2026-11-11 Magpie suggested pairing Codex Security CLI with Kiro's Approve for Me so low-risk fixes land automatically; today's Kiro hooks let scripts answer permission prompts by explicit rule, and Cloudflare's audit skill supplies machine-readable findings those rules can read.
items.context: Auditors generally prefer deterministic, reviewable controls to model-graded ones
chain: The earlier idea relied on the agent grading routine versus risky actions, with no data on how well it separates them.
Hooks now let a script apply a written rule to every permission prompt and rewrite risky tool inputs before execution.
Machine-readable audit findings give the rule something concrete to test, such as finding type or affected path.
Rules are code that auditors can review, so the graded gate becomes easier to approve in regulated settings.
items.who: Application security teams benefit; security tooling budgets pay.
items.variable: Share of routine security fixes merged without manual approval
items.versus: Model-only grading is hard to justify to auditors, and manual review of every fix keeps the backlog growing.
items.smallest_test: Write a hook that auto-approves only one well understood finding category from the audit output, replay recent findings, and succeed if no fix outside that category is approved.
items.disconfirm: Audit findings lack the fields a rule needs, so hooks end up approving almost nothing or nearly everything.

items.title: Coding agent cost cuts stack only if tool pruning keeps cached prefixes stable
items.connection: TokenEconomizer saves money by injecting facts and dropping tools, while Together warns that long sessions depend on stable prompt prefixes, so naive pruning can quietly break the cache.
items.context: Providers price cached input tokens well below uncached ones
chain: TokenEconomizer cut mean cost 18.4% to 30.9% across 277 tasks by changing what goes into the prompt.
Together explains that agents resend full sessions, so any change near the front of the prompt can invalidate the prefix cache.
If tool lists or injected facts change mid-session, the two savings fight each other.
Teams that fix the tool set and facts at session start can likely keep both savings, and harness vendors will need a cache-aware pruning mode.
items.who: Teams running high-volume coding agents on their own or cached APIs benefit; FinOps and platform budgets pay.
items.versus: Adopting either fix alone risks leaving savings on the table or cancelling one with the other, and no existing product claims to coordinate them.
items.smallest_test: Run the same set of repository tasks with TokenEconomizer in default mode and in a frozen-at-start mode while logging cache hit rate; succeed if the frozen mode keeps a clearly higher hit rate and lower total cost.
items.disconfirm: Cache hit rate and total cost are the same in both modes, meaning pruning never touches the cached prefix.

chain: Hooks let a script, not a person, approve or rewrite each tool call in V3 sessions.

items.versus: Without telemetry, scripted approvals are an unverified trust decision, and buying a separate agent-monitoring product duplicates data Kiro now emits.
items.smallest_test: Write one hook that auto-answers file-read prompts, stream telemetry to an existing collector for a week on one team, and succeed if every auto-approved call can be matched to a hook decision with no unexplained calls.
items.disconfirm: Telemetry events cannot be tied to the hook decision that allowed them, so audits cannot tell rule outcomes from manual ones.

viewing.note: Judged from each video's transcript, not its title. Most AI video is recap or hype; these are the exceptions.

items.lead: One set of open weights can now take in molecules, crystals, proteins and sequences alongside code and tool calls.
items.body: SageAI's S2.1 Flash is MIT-licensed and uses tools to check intermediate results. A lab can keep scientific parsing, coding and verification in one model it runs itself. Benchmark leads do not show it will be reliable on your own scientific tasks.

items.lead: Teams can now tune and govern coding agent spend instead of just paying it.
items.body: Microsoft Research's open-source plugin learns from repository sessions to inject short facts, drop unused tools and stop failing loops. Across 277 tasks, mean cost fell 18.4% to 30.9%, and Pass@1 improved in four of five agent-model settings. Kiro's V3 hooks let scripts rewrite tool inputs or answer permission prompts, so team rules cover every call. The savings may not transfer to your repositories, and automated approvals do not prove the rules are safe.

items.lead: Agents are also gaining clearer handoff points to the people who use them.
items.body: AG-UI gives agents and frontend applications a shared protocol boundary. In VS Code, Copilot now shows which agent sessions need attention first, and the Copilot app can reach GitHub Enterprise Server repositories. Neither item establishes adoption or compatibility breadth.
